subject: maths
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is the sum of the interior angles of a triangle?
questions.explain: The interior angles of any triangle always add up to 180°.

questions.q: What is the sum of the exterior angles of any polygon?
options: depends on the number of sides
questions.explain: The exterior angles of any polygon always sum to 360°.

questions.q: The interior angles of a quadrilateral must add up to which total?
questions.explain: A quadrilateral can be split into two triangles, so its interior angles total 2 × 180° = 360°.

questions.q: By the circle theorems, the angle at the centre subtended by an arc is what, compared with the angle at the circumference from the same arc?
questions.explain: The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference subtended by the same arc.

questions.q: What is the size of the angle in a semicircle (the angle subtended at the circumference by a diameter)?
questions.explain: The angle in a semicircle is always a right angle, 90°.

questions.q: To construct the perpendicular bisector of a line segment with compasses, what must you do?
options: Draw arcs of equal radius (more than half the length) from each endpoint
Measure and mark the midpoint with a ruler only
Draw a single arc from one endpoint
Bisect the angle at one end
questions.explain: Equal-radius arcs from both endpoints intersect at two points; the line through them is the perpendicular bisector.

questions.q: The locus of points equidistant from two fixed points A and B is which of the following?
questions.explain: Every point on the perpendicular bisector of AB is the same distance from A as from B.

questions.q: What is the formula for the area of a circle of radius r?
questions.explain: The area of a circle is π multiplied by the radius squared.

questions.q: Which expression gives the circumference of a circle?
questions.explain: The circumference equals 2πr (equivalently πd, where d is the diameter).

questions.q: Which formula correctly gives the volume of a cylinder with base radius r and height h?
questions.explain: A cylinder's volume is the circular base area (πr²) multiplied by its height h.

questions.q: For a right-angled triangle with legs a and b and hypotenuse c, Pythagoras' theorem states:
questions.explain: Pythagoras' theorem relates the squares of the two legs to the square of the hypotenuse.

questions.q: A right-angled triangle has legs of length 6 cm and 8 cm. What is the length of the hypotenuse?
In a right-angled triangle, the sine of an angle is defined as which ratio?
questions.explain: Sine equals the length of the opposite side divided by the hypotenuse (SOH).

questions.q: What is the area of a circle with radius 5 cm (to 1 decimal place)?
questions.explain: Area = πr² = π × 5² = 25π ≈ 78.5 cm².

questions.q: What is the formula for the volume of a sphere of radius r?
questions.explain: The volume of a sphere is four-thirds of π times the radius cubed.

questions.q: A trapezium has parallel sides of 4 cm and 8 cm and a perpendicular height of 5 cm. What is its area?
In a column vector, what does the top number represent?
questions.explain: In a column vector, the top number gives horizontal movement and the bottom number gives vertical movement.

questions.q: To add two column vectors together, you should:
questions.explain: Vectors are added by summing the horizontal components and, separately, the vertical components.

questions.q: What is the magnitude (length) of the vector with components 3 and 4?
If a vector b is equal to 2a, what is true of b compared with a?
options: It is parallel to a and twice its length
It is half the length of a
It points in the opposite direction to a
questions.explain: Multiplying a vector by a positive scalar keeps its direction (parallel) and scales its length by that factor.
